wave_classification_reasons: illiquidity_amihud_daily_xs_rank (cross-sectional percentile rank of the Amihud-inspired daily illiquidity ratio |1-day log return| / same-day dollar volume, i.e. close*volume for that single bar -- NOT a 20-day average dollar volume) has never been used as a ranking/classifier feature in any prior MiniQuantDesk REGISTERED research experiment (ALPHA-01 used momentum_score, SHORT-01 used slope_60, SHORT-WAVE-02/03 used ret_rank_20/ret_5/gap_pct_1, DISCOVERY-01 used vol_rank_20) -- it is the first REGISTERED hypothesis (research_trials/economic-walk-forward identity) in this repo to use trading VOLUME data; the separate, non-registered research-py/experiments/exp_penny screener already uses volume/ADV data outside this hypothesis-registration lineage, so this is not the first use of volume data in the repository's history overall

the economic rationale (illiquidity risk premium) is grounded in primary peer-reviewed literature, not retuned from an observed result: Amihud (2002), 'Illiquidity and Stock Returns: Cross-Section and Time-Series Effects', Journal of Financial Markets 5(1):31-56; Pastor & Stambaugh (2003), 'Liquidity Risk and Expected Stock Returns', Journal of Political Economy 111(3):642-685

the underlying illiquidity_amihud statistic is NOT new code -- it is already unconditionally computed (unranked) by the existing, unmodified mqk_research.features.feature_set_v1.build_feature_set_v1; only the cross-sectional rank transform (identical formula to that same module's own vol_rank_20/atr_rank_14 ranking, applied locally in run_wave.py) is new, and it is a mechanical transform, not new statistical methodology

the seed universe reused here is the SAME current-registry, non-point-in-time 88-symbol snapshot used by SHORT-WAVE-03 and DISCOVERY-01 (see docs/research/BROAD_RESEARCH_UNIVERSE_CURRENT_TRUTH_AUDIT.md) -- carrying the identical survivorship-bias caveat forward unchanged, not a fresh point-in-time-clean universe. A liquidity-premium mechanism specifically requires genuine cross-sectional variation in liquidity, which a fixed liquid-ETF-only universe would suppress by construction -- reusing the broader mixed equity+ETF snapshot is the scientifically appropriate choice here, not a convenience

seed_universe.note: Identical, byte-for-byte reuse of SHORT-WAVE-03's / DISCOVERY-01's own frozen SEED_UNIVERSE.json (same universe_id) -- not regenerated, not re-derived from a possibly-changed live registry. Frozen BEFORE any Wave06 trial result is observed.

LIQ-01.name: single-feature OOS classifier-score cross-sectional rank, Amihud-inspired daily illiquidity / price-impact proxy predictor
primary_references: Amihud (2002), 'Illiquidity and Stock Returns: Cross-Section and Time-Series Effects', Journal of Financial Markets 5(1):31-56
Pastor & Stambaugh (2003), 'Liquidity Risk and Expected Stock Returns', Journal of Political Economy 111(3):642-685
LIQ-01.reference_scope_note: Amihud (2002) establishes a positive return/illiquidity relationship using ILLIQ based on daily absolute-return/dollar-volume ratios AVERAGED over a period. This candidate uses the repo's existing DAILY (same-bar, not period-averaged) ratio followed by a same-date cross-sectional rank and fold-trained classifier -- an Amihud-inspired implementation, not a literal reproduction of the paper's averaged ILLIQ portfolio construction.
LIQ-01.economic_rationale: Investors demand compensation for holding names that are costly to trade (high price impact per dollar traded); the daily |1-day log return| / same-day dollar volume ratio is an Amihud-inspired proxy for that price-impact cost. The classifier's OOS score is trained per fold using illiquidity_amihud_daily_xs_rank as its sole input feature against the SAME fwd_ret>0 binary label used by every prior single-feature family in this repo; the fold-trained logistic regression learns the empirical sign of the illiquidity/forward-return relationship from training data itself -- no direction is hand-asserted here.
LIQ-01.falsification_condition: REJECTED_NOT_ADVANCED per the frozen, machine-checkable advancement_policy in ../wave06_campaign/PREDECLARED_CAMPAIGN.json#/advancement_policy (see verdict_definitions) if the candidate fails any required gate: absolute economic solvency, benchmark-relative excess, matched-placebo excess, primary-vs-control (long-short vs long-only) excess, DSR, PBO, genuine shuffled placebo, robustness gauntlet, or P7A/P7B economic replay stress. No vague terms -- every gate carries an exact frozen numeric threshold or reused literature-standard boundary.

distinctness_from_prior_mechanisms: illiquidity_amihud_daily_xs_rank requires trading VOLUME data (price times volume, i.e. same-day dollar volume) -- no previously tested REGISTERED feature (momentum_score, slope_60, ret_rank_20, ret_5, gap_pct_1, vol_rank_20) uses volume at all; every one of those is a pure price-return or price-level statistic. (The separate, non-registered exp_penny screener elsewhere in this repo already uses volume/ADV data outside this hypothesis-registration lineage.) The economic mechanism (compensation for illiquidity/trading-cost risk, Amihud-inspired / Pastor-Stambaugh 2003) is a fundamentally different risk-factor family from momentum/reversal (behavioral under/overreaction) or the low-volatility/leverage-constraint mechanism already tested and REJECTED_NOT_ADVANCED in DISCOVERY-01 (Ang et al./Frazzini-Pedersen). This is not a retuned parameter variant of any prior family -- it is not a different lookback, threshold, K, universe, or rebalance interval applied to a previously tested statistic.

benchmark.definition: At each economic decision date, equal-weight the SAME causally rankable symbol set available to this family at that date (RANKABLE_SET(T)) -- no future membership, no holdout. Fold-reset semantics identical to SHORT-WAVE-03's/DISCOVERY-01's build_dynamic_rankable_benchmark convention.
benchmark.implementation_status: Already implemented and previously exercised by SHORT-WAVE-03's run_01 and DISCOVERY-01's RISK-01 family (benchmark_type=dynamic_equal_weight_causally_rankable_fold_reset_v1); reused verbatim unchanged in this experiment's run_wave.py (build_dynamic_rankable_benchmark), not reimplemented, not invented after seeing returns.
